## Blocking
- tally/__main__.py:17 — The fix only catches `FileNotFoundError`, but the issue says to "exit 1 if any file could not be read". So `python -m tally somedir good.txt` (`IsADirectoryError`), an unreadable file (`PermissionError`), or a non-UTF-8 file (`UnicodeDecodeError`) still crashes with a traceback and never prints the counts for `good.txt`. Catch `OSError` and use `e.strerror` in the message, and decide how decode errors should be handled.
- tests/test_main.py:17 — The new code isn't tested for the other read failures above (a directory or a file with no read permission). The behaviour the issue asks for ("could not be read" → keep going, exit 1) has no tests beyond the missing-file case.

## Non-blocking
- tests/test_main.py:22 — The test uses the relative path `"nope.txt"`, so it depends on the working directory. If a `nope.txt` exists where the tests run, the test fails. Use a missing path inside the temp dir `d` instead.
- tally/__main__.py:18 — The message text "No such file or directory" is hardcoded. Using `e.strerror` would give the right text for every kind of error.
- tests/test_main.py:27 — There's no test for the case where every file is missing (exit 1, nothing on stdout) or where several files are missing (one stderr line each).
